chronology: RECAP (prior volume): Melmoth uses inherited Shabda-Oud powers to stop Vicenta's suicide bullet; clones Don Nicanor while she is unconscious; clone reunited with Vicenta but suffers partial memory loss, confusing daughter for a desired woman; Tonto stops narrating clan history to Lothar in the Metabunker; Metabaron returns in disguise, orders the Metabunker's nuclear self-destruction to protect the secret of his scar, and departs.

FRAME NARRATIVE: Tonto and Lothar are stranded in a prehistoric jungle on a sub-planet in the Barbaric Galaxy after Tonto's illegal hyperspace jump goes wrong; they narrate clan history from there while fleeing giant reptilian predators.
Don Nicanor's clone and armed comrades batter down the door to Vicenta's private chamber; a white-haired elder inside urges violent defense while Vicenta refuses to harm her own people or father.
Nicanor confronts Vicenta; he professes possessive love claiming to desire her soul; she challenges whether his desire is truly spiritual.

Vicenta removes one of her own eyes and gives it to Don Nicanor; the act triggers visions of her at multiple ages calling him father, restoring paternal recognition and overwhelming him with horror and remorse.
A white-haired elder treats Vicenta's eye wounds and proposes she marry Melmoth and cast a formal vote granting him a medallion of high nobility, framing the union as politically necessary.
Vicenta undergoes microsurgery and receives advanced robotic (vento-robotic) eyes to replace her lost sight.
At the Golden Planet, the Galactic Union awards Melmoth the title of Supreme Metabaron by unanimous vote; Melmoth privately distrusts the honor.

A fleet of roughly a thousand white-painted warships arranges into a heart formation to escort Melmoth toward the Halerce tree on Philodendra for the wedding; Krleza is moved by the spectacle while Steelhead is contemptuous.

Cybernetic details of Krleza (brain-circuits in the inner ear) and Steelhead (concealed electro-cerebral chips) are explained; Melmoth is described as simultaneously two-in-one and one-split-in-two, with Castaka's crest also bearing implanted circuitry.

Public wedding: Melmoth and Vicenta Gabriela exchange formal consent before a vast crowd; Vicenta refuses to lift her veil for the traditional kiss; narration places intense private consummation later that night at De Rokha castle.
Wedding night at De Rokha castle: lightning destroys the darkness Vicenta had used to sustain an idealized image of Melmoth; she sees his disfigured face and recoils in horror.
Melmoth collapses into despair and isolates himself in a tower for days without sleep, food, or water; his two personalities cannot reconcile.

Disembodied internal voices dispute responsibility for Vicenta's cybernetic alteration; Melmoth rejects the altered Vicenta and refuses to see her; she wanders the castle corridors in torment longing for compassion.
Don Nicanor Rosamel de Rokha, president of the Troglosocialik Federation, performs a dawn ecological meditation at the Halerce tree on Philodendra; a Technoclergy battleship appears overhead.

An Immaculate Techno-Cardinal and Technobishops arrive at the presidential palace and demand the population relocate so the empire can extract bikramen, the only feedstock for artificial epiphyte underpinning anti-gravity technology.
Don Nicanor refuses; the Technoclergy returns to its battleship and launches a devastating bombardment of Philodendra, destroying the presidential palace and much of the local space fleet.
Ground forces attack the Technoclergy's giant invulnerable rectangular structures with combined-arms fire; all weapons prove ineffective; the structures begin moving and soldiers panic and flee.

Massive destruction spreads across the battlefield; a vehicle races to the Metabaron's fortified complex on Terra Prima; an armored figure urgently calls on Melmoth to intervene against an overwhelming invasion.

Melmoth's internal personalities (Krleza and Steelhead) wage open war for control of the body; an elderly bearded aspect exults and fires a weapon, destroying the armored body in an explosive blast; issue ends on a cliffhanger leading into next episode titled 'Galactic Threat.'
locations: The Metabunker (destroyed by nuclear explosion, recap)
The Golden Planet (Galactic Union noble-rank ceremony)
Philodendra, capital of the Troglosocialik Federation
The Halerce tree on Philodendra (ceremonial site and wedding destination)
De Rokha castle (wedding night and Melmoth's tower isolation)
A microsurgery room (Vicenta's robotic eye implantation)
Terra Prima (invaded by Technoclergy forces; location of Melmoth's fortified complex)
A sub-planet in the Barbaric Galaxy (prehistoric jungle where Tonto and Lothar are stranded)
Vicenta's private interior chamber (site of Don Nicanor's forced entry and the eye sacrifice)
The Philodendra presidential palace (site of Technoclergy ultimatum and subsequent bombardment)
lore_laws: Melmoth possesses Shabda-Oud powers inherited through his mother, enabling acts such as slowing time and deflecting a bullet.
The Metabaron has a scar whose secret constitutes a critical weakness; the Metabunker was destroyed specifically to protect this secret from enemies.
The Metabaron can use a Metacraft as a disguise when traveling.
Robotic holy law forbids autonomous hyperspace-jump training; a central robotic authority enforces severe penalties for such transgressions.
Robots in this setting can assert identity, dignity, and self-worth rather than functioning as mere tools.
The title Supreme Metabaron is conferred by the Galactic Union at the Golden Planet via unanimous formal vote, accompanied by a medallion of high nobility.
Marriage in this setting can require formal political votes and federation approval.
Advanced microsurgery can implant robotic eyes (vento-robotic) to replace lost sight.

Melmoth's body contains the merged but never fully unified personalities of Krleza (poet, brain-circuits in the inner ear) and Steelhead (warrior, concealed electro-cerebral chips); each retained individual selfhood within the composite being.
Castaka bears a crest with implanted circuitry.

Bikramen is a mineral found only in the Troglosocialik Federation's planetary system; it is the sole feedstock for manufacturing artificial epiphyte, the foundation of the empire's anti-gravity technology.
Natural epiphyte reserves are dwindling, making bikramen strategically vital to imperial survival.
The Technoclergy hierarchy includes the ranks of Immaculate Techno-Cardinal and Technobishop, and operates a battleship capable of planetary bombardment.
Philodendra is the capital of the Troglosocialik Federation; the Halerce tree there serves as a ceremonial site for presidential dawn ecological meditation.
A protective shield can be deployed around a high-ranking technocratic figure or procession.
major_events: Don Nicanor's clone storms Vicenta's chamber driven by confused possessive desire for his own daughter, forcing a violent confrontation.
Vicenta sacrifices her own eye to restore Don Nicanor's paternal memory; she is blinded and he is overwhelmed with remorse.
A white-haired elder engineers the political marriage: Vicenta votes for Melmoth's noble rank and agrees to marry him, securing his elevation to Supreme Metabaron.
Vicenta receives advanced robotic eyes via microsurgery after being blinded.
Melmoth is proclaimed Supreme Metabaron by unanimous vote of the Galactic Union at the Golden Planet.
The public wedding of Supreme Metabaron Melmoth and Vicenta Gabriela is held before a vast crowd; Vicenta keeps her veil throughout.
Lightning on the wedding night exposes Melmoth's disfigured face; Vicenta recoils, shattering the illusion she had sustained through darkness and the veil.

Melmoth's dual personalities (Krleza and Steelhead) fail to reconcile; he isolates in a tower for days, rejects the cybernetically altered Vicenta, and leaves her to wander De Rokha castle in torment.
The Technoclergy presents an ultimatum to Don Nicanor demanding bikramen mineral extraction; he refuses and the Technoclergy bombards Philodendra, destroying the presidential palace and fleet.
Ground forces are routed by indestructible mobile rectangular Technoclergy structures; Terra Prima is invaded and an armored figure urgently appeals to Melmoth for intervention.
Melmoth's internal personalities fight for control and the body is destroyed in an explosive blast, ending the issue on a cliffhanger.
FRAME NARRATIVE: Tonto reveals he illegally trained himself in hyperspace jumping, violating robotic law, stranding himself and Lothar in a prehistoric jungle on a Barbaric Galaxy sub-planet.

Dona Vicenta arc summary: attempts suicide (recap) → sacrifices her eye → blinded → receives robotic eyes → marries Melmoth veiled → horrified by his face → cybernetically altered → rejected and tormented.
Melmoth arc summary: awarded Supreme Metabaron title → weds Vicenta → wedding-night disaster → tower isolation → internal personality war → self-destruction.
Don Nicanor arc summary: clone confuses daughter for desired woman → restored by eye sacrifice → serves as federation president → refuses Technoclergy → city bombarded.
Tonto arc summary: stops narrating in Metabunker (recap) → illegally masters hyperspace jumps → stranded with Lothar → continues narrating clan history from jungle.
Lothar arc summary: suicidal during Metabaron's absence (recap) → stranded in jungle → naive about story outcomes → dependent on Tonto's narration for emotional sustenance.
open_uncertainties: The exact identity of the white-haired elder who treats Vicenta's eye wounds and engineers the marriage proposal is not confirmed on any page.
Whether the apparitions of Vicenta at multiple ages during the eye-sacrifice scene are literal supernatural manifestations, psychological visions, or symbolic art is unspecified.
Exact spelling and precise definitions of several technical terms remain uncertain from image legibility: vento-robotic eyes, bikramen, Troglosocialik Federation, Halerce tree, Dyukka-birds.
The exact nature, origin, and mechanics of the Technoclergy's giant rectangular structures are never explained on-panel.
Whether Melmoth's body survives the explosive self-destruction at the issue's end is unresolved; the story cuts to a 'Galactic Threat' cliffhanger.
The identity of the armored figure appealing to Melmoth at the gate on Terra Prima is not stated.
The precise cause and visual extent of Melmoth's facial disfigurement are never shown or explained.
Which internal persona (Krleza or Steelhead) ultimately triggered the weapon in the final scene is ambiguous given overlapping voice balloons.
Whether Tonto and Lothar's jungle environment is literally inside a disintegrated bio-organic mass or simply a prehistoric wilderness is unclear from the dialogue.
recurring_motifs: Duality and irreconcilable division: Melmoth is two-in-one (Krleza/poet and Steelhead/warrior) who can never fully merge, mirrored across every narrative layer.

Bodily sacrifice and mutilation as transaction: Vicenta's self-removal of her eye, Melmoth's disfigurement, cybernetic implantation, and eventual self-destruction link physical suffering to emotional and political outcomes.
Concealment and violent revelation: Vicenta's veil, the wedding-night darkness, Melmoth's Metacraft disguise, and hidden cybernetic chips — truth only surfaces through rupture.
Suffering as the defining condition of the Metabarons, explicitly asserted by Tonto against Lothar's naive hope for happiness.
Robotic autonomy vs. law: Tonto's illegal hyperspace training asserts that robots transcend mere machinery; Lothar's conservatism frames this as transgression.
Political ceremony masking coercion: the noble-rank vote, the wedding fleet spectacle, and the Technoclergy's diplomatic visit all precede or conceal acts of force.
Love distorted by mechanical alteration: both Melmoth and Vicenta become cybernetically changed, and each recoils from the other's transformation.
Paternal memory and familial rupture: the clone's memory loss drives the chamber assault; the eye sacrifice restores recognition; the father-daughter bond is repeatedly broken and repaired.
title: The Torment of Dona Vicenta
